title: Fewer US Teens Are Taking Summer Jobs
paragraphs: For many years, having a summer job was a normal part of growing up in the US. But today, far fewer American teenagers work during the summer than in the past.

According to an analysis by Pew Research Center, only 35.5% of teens aged 16 to 19 had a paying job for at least part of the summer in 2026. In 1978, the number was 58%, and until about 2000, more than half of teens worked during the summer in most years.

This year's number was actually a little higher than in 2025, when it was 33.8%. However, it is still much lower than in the past. Before the summer, the outplacement company Challenger, Gray & Christmas had even predicted that the number of summer jobs for teens could fall to the lowest level since records began in 1948.

So why are fewer teens working today than in the past? Experts suggest several reasons. First, there are fewer simple, entry-level jobs than in past decades. Second, the school year often ends later and starts earlier than before, and more students take classes during the summer. In addition, many teens do volunteer work or unpaid internships to help them get into college.

For the teens who do work, restaurants and hotels are the most common employers. About 2 million teens, or 32% of working teens, had jobs in this area. Stores were the second most common, employing about 1.3 million teens.
Older teens are much more likely to work than younger ones. About 48% of 18- and 19-year-olds had jobs, compared with only 24% of 16- and 17-year-olds.
Some experts worry that fewer young people are getting early work experience, which can help them build useful skills for the future.
